From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: perf qualification and regional routing / data residency asks

Hi Sana / Amit —

Thanks again for the demo time today — great discussion and appreciate the clear product context. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key performance / SLO topics that matter most to Acme Health and list the immediate follow-ups from our side.

Summary of asks from Acme (as I heard them):
- Latency targets: 95th pct <= 120ms (US), <= 180ms (EU), <= 350ms (APAC) for short-form clinical assistant responses (~<128 tokens).
- Throughput & concurrency: steady 120 reqs/sec, peak bursts to 375 reqs/sec; expected peak concurrency ~80 simultaneous sessions.
- Streaming: server-side streaming for live agent assist (low-latency token streaming) — client expects progressive tokens within 50ms of token generation at the edge.
- Data residency: APAC traffic and all associated logs/telemetry must remain in Singapore region only (no egress to other regions); audit log retention 90d.

Attachments: I attached a quick performance matrix (redwood_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx) with baseline config options and cost estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted protected routing. Also attached a draft SLA for internal review.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
1) Can you confirm the numbers above (latency/throughput/peaks and residency constraints) or flag any corrections?
2) If confirmed, we will:
   - Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week (involving our infra/serving lead + your platform engineer) to align on load shape and streaming protocol.
   - Provision a short-lived dedicated staging pool in US/EU/SG to run a realistic smoke test (we’ll need IP ranges and sample payloads).
   - Share a refined SLO proposal and a recommended routing policy (edge-first, geo-fallback) by EOD Monday.

Please reply with confirmation or edits and available times for the deep-dive.

Thanks —
David
David Kim

Subject: Re: Post-demo: perf qualification and regional routing / data residency asks

Hi David —

Thanks — numbers look close. A few clarifications from our side:
- Latency: Targets are correct for UI responses. For physician-facing real-time assist we would accept slightly higher 95th pct (up to 150ms US) if it materially reduces cost; please flag trade-offs.
- Throughput: Our average is ~120 rps (as you have) but note two weekly peaks for batch clinical review windows where we may see ~420 rps for 10–20 minutes.
- Concurrency: Peak concurrency may reach 120 simultaneous sessions (we under-quoted earlier).
- Streaming: We need server streaming (chunked tokens) with <75ms token-delivery goal at the edge in US/EU; APAC user expectations are looser but still prefer progressive token flow.
- Data residency: Confirmed — APAC must remain in SG only. EU traffic must stay inside EU (Ireland/Frankfurt). US traffic is fine to route to us-west/us-east.

One more ask: logging/PII — we will not allow request bodies with PHI to be stored beyond 12 hours in hosted telemetry. If Dedicated is required for full isolation we want a clear list of differences.

Happy to join the deep-dive; we are available Tue/Wed next week (Mar 9–10) in the afternoon PST.

Best,
Sana Patel
Head of Product — Clinical Platforms
Acme Health
sana.patel@acme.health

Subject: Re: Post-demo: perf qualification and regional routing / data residency asks

Sana —

Thanks for the clarifications — this is super helpful. I captured the updated numbers below and sketched a pragmatic SLO recommendation to balance cost vs latency.

Updated load / residency summary (confirmed):
- Typical steady: 120 rps; weekly bursts up to 420 rps for 10–20m.
- Peak concurrency: 120 sessions.
- Regional split: US 60% / EU 30% / APAC 10% (APAC must remain in SG; EU data in EU).
- Streaming: token delivery goal <75ms in US/EU; APAC best-effort streaming.
- Telemetry/PII: request bodies with PHI must be excluded from hosted retention beyond 12h; Dedicated provides full control for 90d retention inside customer VPC.

Proposed SLOs (initial draft):
- 95th latency (<=128 tokens): US <= 140ms (can target 120ms with dedicated capacity), EU <= 190ms, APAC <= 360ms.
- Error budget / fallback: 99.5% availability per region with automatic fallback to regional compatible model (no egress of APAC traffic).
- Concurrency safety: reserve 140 concurrent slots per region to avoid cold-start/backpressure during peaks.

Operational asks from Acme for the staging test:
1) Sample request payloads and average token sizes (anonymized).
2) Test IP ranges / CIDRs we can add to allowlist for the staging pool.
3) A short list of 10 typical prompts (for quality check and streaming behavior).

Next steps:
- We will provision a 72-hour dedicated staging pool in the requested regions if you approve; the staging config and cost estimate are in the attached spreadsheet.
- Marissa (cc’d) will coordinate the technical deep-dive — tentatively Tue Mar 9 14:00 PST. Please confirm.

If that all sounds good I’ll send a calendar invite and open a short HubSpot ticket with action items.

Thanks —
David
